drafts.after: Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required. Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me, I delight to do thy will, O my God. First principle: God looks for obedience that comes from a heart he has made ready, not for the whole system of sacrifices. Hebrews puts these words in the mouth of the Son as he enters the world.
drafts.reason: split the 27-word abstract sentence; "obedience from a prepared heart" glossed as a heart God makes ready

drafts.after: When man dies, his breath (ruach) departs, he returns to his earth, and in that very day his thoughts perish. Immortality belongs to God alone (1 Tim 6:16). He gives it to the righteous only as a gift at the second coming of Christ (1 Cor 15:51-54). First principle: a person is one whole being, body and breath together (Gen 2:7). When the breath of life leaves, no soul drifts on somewhere else, either in bliss or in torment.
drafts.reason: removed the and-chains and the compressed "psychosomatic unity"; kept every citation and the ruach gloss

drafts.after: Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive: thou hast received gifts for men; yea, for the rebellious also, that the LORD God might dwell among them. His victory parade climbs to the sanctuary and showers the conquered with gifts. First principle: Christ's ascension is a victory march. The spoils he wins, the Spirit and the offices of the church, go to rebels he has made his friends.
drafts.reason: broke the 29-word sentence; "sanctuary" is the frozen glossary rendering; "spoils" defined in place

drafts.after: What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him? For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour. First principle: God meant humanity to rule the earth. Adam lost that rule. We see it fulfilled in Jesus. He was made a little lower for a little while, and now he is crowned, with all things under His feet.
drafts.reason: split the stacked relative clause into one idea per sentence; kept the KJV "visitest" untouched

drafts.after: Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing? The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD, and against his anointed... Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion. First principle: people really do plot against God, and those plots really do fail. God's decree stands: Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee.
drafts.reason: the half-quoted "the decree stands — Thou art my Son" is now one clean quoted line with the app words outside it

drafts.after: False witnesses did rise up; they laid to my charge things that I knew not. They rewarded me evil for good to the spoiling of my soul. The righteous sufferer is tried by perjury. First principle: when truth is on trial, God Himself is the advocate. The charge against the Sufferer was false, and that is exactly what shows he was innocent.
drafts.reason: the 27-word sentence became two; "the point of the charge being false" unpacked without adding a claim

drafts.after: The LORD hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne. The ark's journey to Zion recalls the oath that outlives the exile. First principle: God swears an oath and does not take it back. One of David's own descendants reigns, and Peter preached that God kept the oath in the resurrection (Acts 2:30-31).
drafts.reason: "a physical descendant" made concrete as one of David's own descendants; Acts 2:30-31 kept

drafts.after: They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of mine head... For the zeal of thine house hath eaten me up; and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me. First principle: the Sufferer is hated, and he does nothing to deserve it. He is also eaten up by devotion to God's house. Christ fulfilled both halves, in the temple courts and at the cross.
drafts.reason: separated the two halves of the 24-word sentence into their own sentences; both halves kept

drafts.after: I have set the LORD always before me... Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth: my flesh also shall rest in hope. For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption. First principle: the Holy One goes through the grave and his body does not decay. Peter and Paul both preach the resurrection from this verse.
drafts.reason: "passes through ... without decay" put into plain word order; the hell/corruption quotation untouched

drafts.after: Lift up your heads, O ye gates; and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors; and the King of glory shall come in. Who is this King of glory? The LORD strong and mighty. A warrior-King comes home to his citadel in triumph. First principle: the battle is over, and the King comes home in triumph. Heaven's gates open for the victorious Christ.
drafts.reason: split the stacked clause; kept the citadel image ahead of the meaning

drafts.after: Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows. The Psalm speaks of the King as God, and then speaks of God His God. First principle: the anointed One is himself God, and he is also anointed. The Spirit rests on the Son, and he is glad beyond all his companions.
drafts.reason: loosened the appositive pile-up; kept "divine yet anointed" as the two plain halves it states

drafts.after: Save now, I beseech thee: O LORD, I beseech thee, send now prosperity. Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the LORD. The Hallel psalm that Israel sang at every feast became the street shout when the King rode into Jerusalem. First principle: Israel's psalms put the words of welcome on the people's lips before the King appears.
drafts.reason: named the actor in the 21-word sentence; "street acclamation" eased to "street shout"

drafts.after: The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool. David calls his own descendant my Lord, so this Son is greater than David. First principle: the Messiah is enthroned at God's right hand as both King and Priest (after Melchizedek). His enemies become his footstool in the end.
drafts.reason: split the stacked "as both ... while ..." clause; Melchizedek left as the text already has it

drafts.after: Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me. The betrayal does not come from a stranger. It comes from a man who shared his table. First principle: the deepest hurt of the righteous sufferer is treachery at the table, and Jesus applies the verse to Judas Himself.
drafts.reason: turned the "not from a stranger but from" construction into two plain sentences

drafts.after: David opens Psalm 22 with the cry of a righteous sufferer who has been handed over to judgment. Jesus quotes this exact line from the cross. The psalm moves from that agony to the worship of all nations. First principle: on the cross Christ bore the curse of being forsaken, and he bore it in our place, so that the nations may be gathered to God.
drafts.reason: the 22-word abstract sentence became two and "substitutionary" was written out in plain words

drafts.after: Also I will make him my firstborn, higher than the kings of the earth. My covenant will I not break, nor alter the thing that is gone out of my lips. God adopts David's seed into the rank of firstborn. First principle: the oath to David cannot be broken, and the firstborn holds first place. He is heir of everything, King above every king.
drafts.reason: moved the concrete statement ahead of the abstract "unbreakable"; "preeminent" replaced by "holds first place"

drafts.after: Earthly judges are called gods as children of the Most High. First principle: Jesus reasons from the psalm. If Scripture gave even failing judges that dignity, then the One God set apart and sent cannot be a blasphemer for saying He is the Son.
drafts.reason: the 28-word sentence became two; "the Sanctified and Sent One" rendered in ordinary words

drafts.after: Into thine hand I commend my spirit: thou hast redeemed me, O LORD God of truth. This evening prayer of trusting surrender became the dying words of the Christ. First principle: the righteous hand over their spirit, their times, and their enemies into God's hand, and they confess redemption at the moment they let go.
drafts.reason: straightened the subject-verb order; kept all three objects of the committing in the original order

drafts.after: The throne is built to all generations. First principle: this seed is one person, and the blessing through him is many. Gabriel tells Mary what that means: of His kingdom there shall be no end.
drafts.reason: the 28-word sentence with its colon stack became three sentences, same claims

drafts.after: Reproach hath broken my heart; and I am full of heaviness... They gave me also gall for my meat; and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink. Every kindness refused to the righteous sufferer was written down as a detail of the Passion. First principle: the cross fulfilled scripture down to the drink offered and refused.
drafts.reason: replaced the impersonal passive with an actor; kept the quotation and the claim intact

drafts.after: The throne lasting as the sun before God. First principle: the people asked whether Christ is David's son. The psalm answers that the throne outlasts the sun, and Hebrews gives that throne to the Son.
drafts.reason: split the 27-word sentence; kept the sun image and the Hebrews claim

drafts.after: I became also a reproach unto them: when they looked upon me they shaked their heads. The scorned sufferer becomes a byword among mockers. First principle: ridicule was part of what the Passion was foretold to include. Even the gesture of the head was written down before Golgotha.
drafts.reason: the abstract "predicted instrument" clause became a plain statement; the quotation is untouched

drafts.after: The rest-forfeiting oath. First principle: this oath cuts both ways. The promise stands for believers, and the exclusion stands for unbelief. The rest remains for the people of God.
drafts.reason: replaced the two semicolon-joined clauses with one idea per sentence

drafts.after: Glory refused to self, assigned to mercy and truth. First principle: this is the engine behind all witness. The name gets the credit. Jesus refused glory that belonged to the Father, and he did it in the same spirit.
drafts.reason: split the dash-joined sentence and named the actor; kept "the name gets the credit" as the point

drafts.after: The Bible's shortest psalm is its widest invitation. First principle: two verses make the Gentiles a choir. Paul strings it into the Romans 15 chain and proves that Gentile praise was always the plan.
drafts.reason: the 25-word clause chain became three sentences; the Romans 15 claim is unchanged

drafts.after: Corn of heaven in the wilderness. First principle: this psalm supplies the question the crowd later puts to Jesus, and this is His answer: Moses gave not the bread; my Father gives the true bread.
drafts.reason: replaced the compressed "feeds the crowd's question to Jesus" with a plain subject-verb-object clause

drafts.after: Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but the LORD delivereth him out of them all. He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken. The righteous sufferer goes through affliction with an unbroken body, which is the Passover-lamb pattern. First principle: God keeps His sacrifice whole even in death.
drafts.reason: loosened the appositive; kept the Passover-lamb image and named it before its meaning

drafts.after: The decree is declared to the Son Himself. First principle: begotten is a status decree, not a birthday. Paul and Hebrews apply it to the resurrection and to the eternal generation alike.
drafts.reason: one idea per sentence; both applications kept

drafts.after: The world and its dwellers belong to God. First principle: because God owns it all, worship and right living both rest on that. Paul quotes it against the fear of idol-food. The earth is the Father's, and the Son governs it.
drafts.reason: split the semicolon clause; "ownership grounds worship and ethics" said in everyday words

drafts.after: The King is addressed as God with an eternal right sceptre. First principle: the Father Himself speaks to the Son as God. Hebrews reads the psalm as God speaking directly about the Son's throne.
drafts.reason: named the speaker; "direct divine speech" replaced with plain words

drafts.after: Wrongful enemies must not win the day. First principle: John ties the phrase to the world's hatred of Christ. The causeless hatred of the Righteous One was prophesied twice over.
drafts.reason: split the 24-word sentence; both witnesses to the prophecy kept

drafts.after: The psalm of the Holy One's confidence: at my right hand, I shall not be moved. First principle: Peter preaches this as Christ's own settled trust. It is the resurrection certainty of the One at God's right hand.
drafts.reason: the dash clause became its own sentence; no claim lost

drafts.after: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner. This is the LORD's doing; it is marvellous in our eyes. Rejection by the builders becomes God's appointment. First principle: exaltation follows rejection. The crucified One is the foundation of all God's building.
drafts.reason: separated the two claims that one semicolon had joined; "professionals" made concrete as "builders"

drafts.after: Adamic dominion is the psalm's theme; Hebrews finds it exhausted in Christ. First principle: the dominion Adam lost is visible again in the crowned Son. All things are under his feet, though we do not yet see them all.
drafts.reason: split the semicolon sentence and put the last clause in plain word order

drafts.after: The rulers take counsel against the LORD and against His anointed. First principle: the conspiracy of Psalm 2 met at Calvary. Herod, Pilate, and the nations did exactly this, exactly as it was foretold.
drafts.reason: the 22-word sentence became three; all three named conspirators kept

drafts.after: Heaven, hell, the dawn, the sea — the Spirit is there. First principle: God is present everywhere, and that is both comfort and inescapability. Nowhere is God absent, and for the believer who is being chased that is good news.
drafts.reason: the two abstract nouns unpacked into one plain sentence each

drafts.after: The mockers quote the Sufferer's own faith back at Him. First principle: at the cross the taunt He trusted in God; let Him deliver Him now was fulfilled line for line.
drafts.reason: removed the dash parenthesis so the quotation reads as one line; "line-for-line fulfillment" kept

drafts.after: The Word lights each next step on a dark road. First principle: guidance comes a step at a time, like a lamp and not a floodlight. Peter uses the same image and calls prophecy the surer light.
drafts.reason: split the 22-word sentence; kept the lamp-versus-floodlight contrast

drafts.after: The Son's inheritance includes shattering rebel powers like pottery. First principle: the same rod promised to Messiah is handed to those who overcome. Iron rule belongs to the faithful, not to the faithless.
drafts.reason: one idea per sentence; "delegated to overcomers" put into everyday words

drafts.after: The patriarchs are God-protected sojourners. First principle: God guards the covenant line all through danger. The anointed ones and the prophets carry a promise that taught the nations to be afraid.
drafts.reason: covenant line kept and the agent named; the fear-of-the-nations claim preserved

drafts.after: Guardian angels bear up the trusting one in all his ways. First principle: Satan quoted this at the temptation. The promise is for the path of obedience, never for testing God.
drafts.reason: split the dash clause; both halves of the claim kept

drafts.after: The Hallel cry for salvation and prosperity. First principle: on Palm Sunday, Hosanna was this verse on people's lips. The request had become a shout of welcome for the coming King.
drafts.reason: two ideas in one 22-word sentence separated; "acclamation" said plainly

drafts.after: Solomon's greater Son rules to the ends of the earth. First principle: this royal psalm reaches past every Israelite king. The kingdom that fills the earth belongs to the Son, and it lasts forever.
drafts.reason: the 21-word sentence with its dash became three plain sentences

drafts.after: Man's rage does not cancel God's decree: My King is installed on Zion. First principle: God's decree stands over the conspiracy. The cross that men meant as rejection, God meant as enthronement.
drafts.reason: the colon-chained sentence separated; the cross/enthronement claim kept whole

drafts.after: He names every star — great power, understanding infinite. First principle: the one who counts the stars is the one who heals the brokenhearted. The same power that orders the skies binds up wounds.
drafts.reason: split the 21-word sentence and replaced the "both" construction with a plain statement

drafts.after: The sun-pavilion preaches day and night to the ends of the world. First principle: creation's voice reaches everyone and uses no words. Paul takes it as the pattern for how far the gospel's sound goes.
drafts.reason: "universal and wordless" written out; "adopts" eased to "takes"

drafts.after: Green pastures, still waters, the valley, the table — the Shepherd psalm. First principle: the LORD who shepherds his people is the Lamb who feeds them. Christ claims the psalm, and heaven fulfills it.
drafts.reason: made the two subjects explicit instead of leaving "the LORD who shepherds is the Lamb who feeds" compressed

drafts.after: The memorial-name spans all generations. First principle: the name God revealed at the bush is the name his people remember at every altar. He stays the same, and that is part of what he promised.
drafts.reason: the abstract "permanence is part of the promise" rewritten as two plain statements

drafts.after: The Maker keeps truth forever. First principle: trust belongs to the Creator, not to princes. The psalm grounds hope in the same making power Paul preaches to idolaters.
drafts.reason: named the actor; the Creator-not-princes contrast kept

drafts.after: The oath out of God's lips is unalterable. First principle: even when David's line broke faith, it could not void the word. The promise survives, and Christ is where it is fulfilled.
drafts.reason: the 21-word sentence with a dash split into two; "covenant failure in David's line" said plainly

drafts.after: Experience is invited: taste and see; blessed is the trusting man. First principle: Peter applies the tasting to the Lord Himself. Newborn babes long for the milk because they have tasted it.
drafts.reason: the 20-word sentence split into three; the newborn-babe image kept

drafts.after: The perishing heavens versus the enduring Creator. First principle: Hebrews addresses the Son with this psalm. The Maker of creation is the unchanging Person whose years have no end.
drafts.reason: the 21-word sentence split; "creation's Maker" rephrased with the same claim

drafts.after: God ordains strength from infant lips to still the enemy. First principle: perfect praise comes from the least likely people. The children shouting Hosanna quoted this psalm back at the establishment.
drafts.reason: the dash clause became its own sentence; kept the Hosanna detail

drafts.after: The ascent question demands clean hands and a pure heart. First principle: only purity sees God. The beatitude and the epistle both answer the question with Christ's own holiness.
drafts.reason: split the dash clause; all three witnesses kept

drafts.after: Devouring zeal and fallen reproaches — both quoted of Christ. First principle: the cleansing of the temple and the insults of the cross come from the same psalm, and they belong to the same man.
drafts.reason: split the compound; "the same psalm, the same Man" written out as a full clause

drafts.after: It speaks of an ear dug open, which marked willing servanthood (Exod 21:6). Hebrews reads it as a body prepared for the will of God (Heb 10:5).
drafts.reason: removed the 23-word sentence fragment and the coined "bored-open"; both citations kept

drafts.after: David confesses God among the nations. First principle: Paul quotes this to prove the plan always included Gentile praise. The victory song of David was prophecy about mission.
drafts.reason: split the dash clause; "Davidic victory song was mission prophecy" said in plain words

drafts.after: The confession joins generations in guilt. First principle: shared history means shared accountability. The prayer that names ancestral sin honestly is the prayer that finds mercy.
drafts.reason: the semicolon-joined abstract pair separated; each idea now stands alone

drafts.after: Asaph's dark sayings of old are Jesus' teaching method. First principle: the parables are not a backup plan. They are the psalm's own program for revealing and for concealing.
drafts.reason: split the dash clause and replaced the jargon "plan B"

drafts.after: Man can do nothing ultimate against the LORD-sided soul. First principle: courage is arithmetic. The greater Helper outweighs every human threat. Hebrews makes this the cure for loving money.
drafts.reason: split the dash clause; "antidote to covetousness" put in everyday words

drafts.after: A lamp ordained for the anointed; David's horn sprouts. First principle: the resting-place God chose grows a light. Zacharias' horn of salvation and the dawn of David's house both sprout from here.
drafts.reason: split the semicolon pairs; kept both Zacharias and house-of-David claims

drafts.after: God needs nothing from sacrificial hands — the world is already His. First principle: God wants thanksgiving, not people feeding heaven. The animals on a thousand hills are already His.
drafts.reason: the semicolon compound split; the a-thousand-hills clause kept in its KJV shape

drafts.after: Earth and heaven are summoned to a name above the terrain. First principle: the praise of all creation in Psalm 148 rehearses the final doxology to the enthroned Lamb.
drafts.reason: the 19-word sentence simplified; "universal praise" made concrete as "the praise of all creation"

drafts.after: The chosen-covenant oath is struck with David. First principle: every throne promise in the New Testament rests on this sworn covenant. Sworn mercy is unbreakable mercy.
drafts.reason: the dash clause became its own sentence; the final maxim kept as it stands

drafts.after: The covered-sin psalm of forgiven David. First principle: this is Paul's proof-text for righteousness credited to a person. Blessedness comes not from works but from the Lord not imputing iniquity.
drafts.reason: glossed "imputed" as "credited", which is the same claim; the KJV clause is untouched

drafts.after: David's deliverance song stacks the titles: rock, fortress, deliverer, horn of salvation. First principle: every rescue title David used is fulfilled in the greater Son. He is the horn lifted up for us.
drafts.reason: split the dash clause; kept all four titles and the horn claim

drafts.after: Every righteous judgment endures forever. First principle: the whole collection of God's words can be trusted at once. Jesus prays Thy word is truth over the entire witness.
drafts.reason: "corpus" and "trustworthy" replaced with everyday words; the prayer kept

drafts.after: Homage or wrath — Blessed are all they that put their trust in him. First principle: the psalm ends with an invitation. The Lamb who is angry is also the refuge of the soul that trusts him.
drafts.reason: the 17-word sentence split; "gospel invitation" said plainly

drafts.after: Adder-poison under the lips. First principle: the way the psalms describe evil speech becomes the evidence Paul presents in court. The mouth is what convicts the human race.
drafts.reason: the 20-word sentence split; "anatomy", "courtroom exhibit" and "the race" put into everyday words

drafts.after: The deserted dwelling and another taking office. First principle: Peter joins this psalm to Judas. The field and the office he forfeited both fulfill this psalm of imprecation.
drafts.reason: split the dash clause; "imprecation" defined by the sentence it now sits in

drafts.after: Joseph sold as a servant, positioned ahead of famine. First principle: providence goes first. God sends the savior into Egypt before the family knows it needs one.
drafts.reason: split the dash clause; "providence precedes" turned into a plain sentence

drafts.after: The betrayer's days are few and his office forfeited. First principle: Peter quotes it when the twelfth witness is chosen. Prophecy governs even the apostolic succession after a betrayal.
drafts.reason: the dash clause became a sentence and the actor is named

drafts.after: The word of the LORD tried Joseph until it proved him out. First principle: tested promises have an appointed release. The dream was fulfilled at the exact moment the prison door opened.
drafts.reason: split the dash clause; made "the prison-door moment" a concrete scene

drafts.after: The imprecation of the Sufferer: welfare turned trap. First principle: Paul applies the table-snare to unbelieving Israel. Safety itself becomes judgment where Messiah is refused.
drafts.reason: the colon-chained first sentence separated from the principle; both claims kept

drafts.after: The LORD's unrepented oath installs the eternal priest. First principle: the oath outlasts Aaron. Hebrews builds its whole argument for the priesthood on this single unchangeable line.
drafts.reason: split the 18-word sentence; "entire priesthood argument" made plain

drafts.after: Clothes divided, lots cast — written a millennium before the soldiers. First principle: the soldiers gambling at the cross did not know they were acting out Psalm 22.
drafts.reason: the 17-word sentence split; "the gambling squad" replaced with a plain description

drafts.after: Sheep of His hand are summoned: To day if ye will hear his voice. First principle: the flock has a Shepherd and a Today. When hearing is put off, the heart grows hard.
drafts.reason: split the colon-chained sentence; "hearing delayed is heart hardened" written out in full

drafts.after: Idol-boasters are confounded while heaven's order worships the true One. First principle: Hebrews quotes it of the Son's advent. The first-begotten receives what idol-worshipers lose.
drafts.reason: split the 16-word sentence and named what heaven's order does

drafts.after: Matthew uses the same gesture of the passers-by at the cross (Matt 27:39). It is mockery in a Hebrew posture.
drafts.reason: the dash-appended fragment became a sentence of its own

drafts.after: Rabbinic sources (Shemoth Rabba) apply the psalm to Messiah. The entry is His heavenly welcome, not an earthly parade.
drafts.reason: split the semicolon into two sentences; "reception" eased to "welcome"

drafts.after: Here it is bitterness pressed to the lips of the Sufferer (Matt 27:34). John records the vinegar carried on hyssop.
drafts.reason: split the semicolon; "hyssop-borne" written out in plain words

drafts.after: The mocked Sufferer foresees the crowd at Golgotha shooting out the lip. First principle: mockery is part of the Passion script. Rulers sneering is prophecy being performed.
drafts.reason: the 15-word sentence split; "lip-shooting" untangled into the gesture it names

drafts.after: The character-proclamation of Exodus 34 in psalm form. First principle: mercy in abundance is how God describes himself. Scripture says it again and again, and Christ shows it in person.
drafts.reason: split the 15-word sentence; "plenteous mercy" and "embodied" put into everyday words

drafts.after: Eccl 12:7 — spirit returns to God who gave it. It is the life-giving power, not an independent ghost.
drafts.reason: split the dash clause; "animating principle" said in plain words

drafts.after: Aramaic in Matt 27:46: Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani — Christ's loud cry at the ninth hour. He cried it out aloud.
drafts.reason: removed the dash fragment; the Aramaic words and Matt 27:46 kept unchanged

drafts.after: The Sanhedrin sought such testimony against Jesus. The law required two witnesses who agreed (Matt 26:59-61).
drafts.reason: the and-joined 16-word sentence split; both halves kept

drafts.after: Acts 2:31 renders it hades, and it insists that David's tomb still holds him while Christ's does not.
drafts.reason: loosened the compression; the hades rendering and both tombs kept

drafts.after: Delight in the LORD ends in abundance of peace. First principle: this is where the second beatitude comes from. The meek inherit, and those who grab lose. Christ blesses the very people the world overlooks.
drafts.reason: separated the semicolon pair into two sentences; all three claims kept

drafts.after: The fall: at death the body goes back to dust and the breath goes back to God.
drafts.reason: split the and-joined clause; agent and direction named

drafts.after: The creation formula: man does not have a soul that lives on by itself. Man became a living soul.
drafts.reason: split the semicolon clause and the abstract "possess an independent immortal soul"

drafts.after: The apostolic hope: at the second coming, which is heard and seen, believers are woken from sleep, all together.
drafts.reason: the passage really does teach one audible, visible coming and believers raised together, so both claims stay

drafts.after: Scripture agrees: in death there is no awareness, no praise, and no communication.
drafts.reason: the abstraction "Canonical consensus" replaced with a plain subject and verb

drafts.after: The starting point: immortality belongs to God alone. For human beings it is conditional.
drafts.reason: the abstraction "Theological baseline" replaced; both halves kept

drafts.after: God cleans up the whole universe: sin, death, and the grave are destroyed forever.
drafts.reason: the abstraction "Cosmic cleansing" replaced with a plain actor and verb

drafts.after: This is the earliest clear hope that a person will see God in the body after the body has fallen apart.
drafts.reason: the nominal pile-up "explicit hope of bodily vision of God after physical dissolution" unpacked

drafts.after: Paul quotes Isaiah 25:8 and Hosea 13:14 to prove the bodily resurrection.
drafts.reason: named the actor and the purpose; both citations kept

drafts.after: The dead are not conscious at all. Thinking and awareness stop completely at death.
drafts.reason: the abstraction "Total unconsciousness" replaced with a plain sentence

drafts.after: The change: the body is made incorruptible at the resurrection, not at death.
drafts.reason: straightened word order; "transformation" and "bestowed" simplified

drafts.after: God destroys the wicked completely in the final fire. They are not tortured forever.
drafts.reason: removed the abstract headings and put the claim in plain subject-verb order

drafts.after: Same-OT: a specific prophecy that his body would be pierced and his clothes divided.
drafts.reason: removed the abstract nouns "physical piercing" and "garment division"

drafts.after: Same-OT: the righteous one suffers and is offered a bitter drink.
drafts.reason: split the compressed participial phrase into a plain clause

drafts.after: Peter applies Isaiah 53 to what Christ did in our place.
drafts.reason: named the actor; "substitutionary work" said in everyday words

drafts.after: Same-OT: the earth gives up its dead in the resurrection.
drafts.reason: removed the abstract "casting forth" construction

drafts.after: Same-OT: YHWH pays the price to bring his people back from the power of the grave.
drafts.reason: replaced the rare "ransoming" but kept the KJV phrase "from the power of the grave" word for word

drafts.after: The pierced King appears at the end of the story.
drafts.reason: replaced "eschatological manifestation" with the glossary rendering for the last days

drafts.after: Same-OT: he chose to submit to public shame and violence.
drafts.reason: named the actor instead of leaving the sentence subjectless

drafts.after: Same-OT: the Shepherd, who is YHWH's close Companion, is struck down.
